nodes.title: React UI (components + routes)
nodes.summary: Every screen and widget: the board canvas, columns, notes, voting and timer dialogs, settings, login screens. Routes wire them to URLs; components read state with useAppSelector and mutate it by dispatching actions.
constraints: Most components dispatch an action and let store middleware do the I/O, but four call the API directly: SettingsDialog/Feedback, Timer, NewBoard and ExportBoard/PrintView.
LoginProviders renders Google and Microsoft buttons only, even though the server supports five providers.

nodes.title: Redux store (actions + reducers)
nodes.summary: Redux Toolkit store. One reducer per domain slice (board, columns, notes, reactions, participants, requests, votes, votings, auth, view, skinTone) combined in store/index.ts.
constraints: A parseMiddleware wrapper stamps action.context (user, board, voting, serverTimeOffset) onto every action before the reducers see it.
Side effects run in the middleware's finally block, so the reducer has already applied the action when the API call is made.

nodes.title: Store middleware (side effects + websocket)
nodes.summary: The only place in the frontend that performs I/O. Each pass*Middleware function matches on action.type and calls the API; board.tsx additionally owns the single board websocket and dispatches server events back into the store.
constraints: One module-level `socket` variable holds the board connection; PermittedBoardAccess opens it, LeaveBoard closes it.
There are two websockets, not one: board.tsx holds the board socket and request.tsx holds a second socket for join-request updates.
Failed writes surface as a Toast with a retry button that re-dispatches the same action — there is no request queue.

nodes.title: REST client modules
nodes.summary: One module per resource, each a plain object of async fetch() calls against SERVER_HTTP_URL. api/index.ts spreads them all into a single flat `API` object.
constraints: Authenticated calls pass credentials: "include" — auth is the HttpOnly `jwt` cookie, never an Authorization header. The public /info call in info.ts omits it.
Non-2xx responses are turned into thrown Errors here, not returned as values.

nodes.title: Frontend platform (entry, config, types, i18n, utils)
nodes.summary: index.tsx mounts the app; config.ts resolves the server and websocket URLs; types/ holds the shared DTOs including the websocket event union; i18n/ holds the en and de translation bundles.
constraints: Runtime config comes from cookies first (scrumlr__server-url, scrumlr__websocket-url), then REACT_APP_* env vars, then window.location — so one built image serves every environment.
types/websocket.ts is the hand-maintained mirror of the Go BoardEventType constants; adding a server event means editing it too.

nodes.title: Server bootstrap (main.go)
nodes.summary: The composition root. Parses CLI flags / env / TOML with urfave/cli, migrates the database, picks Redis or NATS for the broker, builds every service and hands them to api.New().
constraints: Wiring is manual constructor injection — there is no DI container, so a new service means editing main.go and api.New().
The process refuses to start without a private key unless the `insecure` flag is set.
If redis-address is set it wins over the NATS URL; otherwise NATS is used.

nodes.title: HTTP + websocket API (chi)
nodes.summary: chi router with a public group (/info, /health, /feedback, /login/*) and a JWT-protected group (/boards, /boards/{id}/**, /user). Also upgrades and serves the per-board websocket and the join-request websocket.
constraints: Authorization is middleware, not handler code: BoardParticipantContext / BoardModeratorContext / BoardEditableContext / BoardCandidateContext decide who may call what.
POST /boards/{id}/participants is rate limited to 3 requests per 5 seconds per IP.
Board subscriptions live in in-process maps on the Server struct, so a horizontally scaled deployment relies on the broker, not on sticky state.

nodes.title: Auth (JWT + OAuth providers)
nodes.summary: Signs and verifies ES512 JWTs, and registers the goth OAuth providers that were configured at startup. Also exposes AuthContext, which puts the caller's user id into the request context.
constraints: A provider is only registered when its client id, secret and the auth-callback-host are all set — an unset provider simply does not appear.
JWTs are ES512 (ECDSA); the `unsafe-key` flag exists to rotate off an old key by verifying with both.
devkeys/ holds an embedded keypair used only under the `insecure` flag.
The two login paths issue different cookie lifetimes: anonymous gets MaxAge math.MaxInt32, the OAuth callback gets a three-week expiry.

nodes.title: Domain services
nodes.summary: Business logic per domain: boards (incl. columns, timer, export), notes, reactions, board_reactions, votings, users, feedback, health. services.go declares the interfaces the API depends on.
constraints: Mutating methods write to the database and then broadcast the new state on the board channel — the HTTP response is not how other clients learn about a change. The broadcast is not always in the obvious file: vote changes are broadcast from notes.go, and votings/votes.go broadcasts nothing itself.
Services depend on narrow local DB interfaces (e.g. notes.DB), not on *database.Database, which is what makes them unit-testable.
Internal errors are mapped to common.InternalServerError before leaving the service; raw driver errors are logged, not returned.

nodes.title: Data access + migrations (bun)
nodes.summary: bun ORM over PostgreSQL. One file per table (boards, columns, notes, votes, votings, reactions, sessions, session requests, users) plus the embedded SQL migrations run at startup.
constraints: Connection pool is sized 4 * GOMAXPROCS for both max-open and max-idle.
Migrations are numbered up/down SQL pairs under migrations/sql and are applied by the server on boot, not by a separate job.
database.Get() loads a whole board (board, requests, sessions, columns, notes, reactions, votings, votes) in one call — that is what the websocket INIT event is built from.

nodes.title: Realtime broker abstraction
nodes.summary: One Client interface with two implementations, NATS and Redis pub/sub. Broker.BroadcastToBoard publishes a BoardEvent; GetBoardChannel subscribes and returns a Go channel the websocket handler drains.
constraints: BoardEventType is the contract with the frontend; the browser's types/websocket.ts must be updated in lockstep.
Subjects are derived, not configured — boardsSubject(boardID) builds the channel name from the board UUID.
Neither backend persists events: a client that is disconnected during a broadcast recovers only by reconnecting and reading the INIT snapshot.

nodes.title: Server platform (dto, errors, logging, context keys)
nodes.summary: Shared plumbing: the dto package that defines every JSON payload, the filter types, HTTP error helpers, cookie sealing, the zap logger and the typed context-key identifiers.
constraints: Context values are read through the identifiers constants, never through raw strings.

common.SealCookie sets HttpOnly always, adds Secure + SameSite=Strict only when the request protocol is https, and pins Domain to the top-level host — so local http and deployed https share one code path.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: System of record for boards, columns, notes, reactions, votes, votings, sessions and users. Schema lives in 28 numbered up/down SQL migration files.
constraints: The connection URL is a single env var, SCRUMLR_SERVER_DATABASE_URL; there is no read replica split.

nodes.title: NATS (default broker)
nodes.summary: Default pub/sub transport for board events. Used unless a Redis address is configured.
constraints: Core NATS, not JetStream — messages are fire-and-forget with no replay.

nodes.title: Redis pub/sub (alternative broker)
nodes.summary: Drop-in replacement for NATS. Selected when SCRUMLR_SERVER_REDIS_HOST is set.
constraints: Both transports carry JSON: this path marshals by hand in encodeEvent, the NATS path uses nats.NewEncodedConn(nc, nats.JSON_ENCODER).

nodes.title: OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Azure AD, Apple)
nodes.summary: Identity providers reached through markbates/goth. Each is optional and only registered when its credentials are configured.
constraints: Callback URLs are built as {auth-callback-host}{base-path}/login/{provider}/callback — the provider console must match exactly.

nodes.title: Feedback webhook (Slack-shaped)
nodes.summary: POST target for the in-app feedback form. The payload is a hand-built Slack blocks JSON body with German copy.
constraints: Unset SCRUMLR_FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_URL disables the feature via Enabled(); it is not an error state.

nodes.title: Plausible analytics
nodes.summary: Optional, self-hostable pageview tracking. Only initialised when both the analytics domain and host cookies are present.
constraints: Board ids are SHA-256 hashed before the pageview URL is sent, so board identifiers never reach the analytics host.

nodes.title: Build, packaging and deployment
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Dockerfiles for frontend and server, the nginx image that serves the built SPA, docker-compose for local self-hosting, Kubernetes manifests and Terraform for the SKE cluster, and the GitHub Actions workflows.
constraints: nginx injects runtime config into the SPA as Set-Cookie headers on /index.html; that is why one frontend image works across environments.
index.html is served with no-store while JS/JSON get 3 days and media 14 days — a stale index.html would pin clients to an old bundle.

nodes.title: Documentation site (Astro Starlight)
nodes.summary: Separate yarn workspace holding the getting-started, development and self-hosting docs. Published to GitHub Pages.
constraints: It has its own package.json and yarn.lock — installing the root dependencies does not install the docs ones.

edges.note: Server websocket events are dispatched straight back into the store.
Four components bypass the middleware and call the API directly.
Schema migrations are applied in-process at boot, before the HTTP server starts.
nginx sets the runtime-config cookies that src/config.ts reads on load.
Every server flag is supplied as a SCRUMLR_* environment variable by the deployment.

flows.name: Anonymous user opens a board
flows.trigger: Someone opens /board/{id} without an existing session.

steps.detail: RequireAuthentication sends the visitor to LoginBoard; handleLogin calls Auth.signInAnonymously(displayName) and then sets window.location.pathname back to the board.
utils/auth.ts calls API.signInAnonymously and dispatches Actions.signIn on success.
POST /login/anonymous.
signInAnonymously creates the user, signs an ES512 JWT and sets it as an HttpOnly `jwt` cookie with MaxAge math.MaxInt32.
AuthConfiguration.Sign issues the token; the protected routes later verify it via jwtauth.
Back on /board/{id}, BoardGuard dispatches Actions.joinBoard(boardId).
passRequestMiddleware calls API.joinBoard and branches on the returned status: ACCEPTED, PENDING, PASSPHRASE_REQUIRED, WRONG_PASSPHRASE, REJECTED, BANNED or TOO_MANY_JOIN_REQUESTS.
POST /boards/{id}/participants — rate limited to 3 requests per 5 seconds per IP.
BoardSessions.Create creates the session, or a pending board_session_request.
User and session rows committed.

flows.outcome: On ACCEPTED the store dispatches permittedBoardAccess, which is what opens the board websocket. PENDING instead opens the join-request socket in request.tsx and waits for a moderator.

flows.name: Board websocket opens and receives its INIT snapshot
flows.trigger: The store dispatches PermittedBoardAccess after the join succeeds.

steps.detail: passBoardMiddleware opens `new Socket(${SERVER_WEBSOCKET_URL}/boards/{id})`.
openBoardSocket upgrades the connection and calls boards.FullBoard for the snapshot.
Boards.FullBoard assembles board, columns, notes, reactions, votings, votes, sessions and requests.
database.Get() loads the whole board in one pass.
Rows read.
Sends the INIT event, then subscribes to the board channel via GetBoardChannel.
SubscribeToBoardEvents binds the broker subject for this board id.
The INIT message is dispatched as Actions.initializeBoard and populates every slice.

flows.outcome: The client holds a full board snapshot and is subscribed to further board events.

flows.name: Adding a note fans out to every participant
flows.trigger: A participant submits text in NoteInput.

steps.detail: NoteInput dispatches Actions.addNote(columnId, content).
passNoteMiddleware calls API.addNote; a failure raises a Toast with a retry button.
POST /boards/{id}/notes with credentials included.
POST /boards/{id}/notes runs under BoardParticipantContext plus BoardEditableContext before createNote calls the service.
NoteService.Create inserts the note, then calls UpdatedNotes for the board.
CreateNote writes the row and re-reads the board's notes.
Note row committed.
BroadcastToBoard publishes a NOTES_UPDATED BoardEvent on the board subject.
Default transport fans the event out to every subscribed server instance.
Each board subscription writes the event to its websocket clients.
passBoardMiddleware dispatches Actions.updatedNotes and every open board re-renders.

flows.outcome: All participants see the new note; the author's own view updates from the broadcast, not from the POST response.

flows.name: OAuth sign-in with an external provider
flows.trigger: A visitor picks Google / GitHub / Microsoft / Azure AD / Apple on the login screen.

steps.detail: LoginProviders renders a button per enabled provider (Google and Microsoft only) and calls Auth.signInWithAuthProvider.
utils/auth.ts sets window.location.href to ${SERVER_HTTP_URL}/login/{provider}?state={originURL}.
beginAuthProviderVerification hands off to gothic for the provider redirect.
initializeProviders registered only the providers whose client id, secret and callback host were configured.
The provider authenticates the user and redirects to {callback-host}{base-path}/login/{provider}/callback.
verifyAuthProviderCallback runs gothic.CompleteUserAuth, then switches on the provider to pick the right Create*User call.
users.CreateGoogleUser (or the sibling per provider) upserts the account.
User and account rows persisted.

flows.outcome: A three-week jwt cookie is set and the handler replies 303 to the state URL the client sent, or to the app root.

flows.name: In-app feedback reaches the team webhook
flows.trigger: A user submits the feedback form in the settings dialog.

steps.detail: The SettingsDialog Feedback panel collects type, contact and text and calls FeedbackAPI.sendFeedback directly — this one does not go through the store.
POST /feedback — a public route, no JWT required.
createFeedback rejects an unknown feedback type, defaults empty contact/text to "/", and rejects an empty BUG_REPORT or FEATURE_REQUEST body.
FeedbackService.Create builds a Slack blocks JSON body and POSTs it.
The configured webhook receives the message.

flows.outcome: Feedback lands in the team's channel. With SCRUMLR_FEEDBACK_WEBHOOK_URL unset, Enabled() reports false, GET /info returns feedbackEnabled: false and the Feedback panel renders nothing.
